item.description:

The evening will provide an opportunity for residents, fair supporters, exhibitors, volunteers, community partners, and the public to connect directly with Fair leadership, share ideas, ask questions, and discuss the future of the Solano County Fair.
The meeting will begin with introductory remarks from CEO Tom Keaney, followed by an open session and public comment. The focus of the evening will be on hearing directly from the community about what they value most, what they'd like to see in the years ahead, and how the Fair can continue to grow as a cherished tradition for Solano County.

item.title: Max Vogel + The Pickups — Fri Jul 31, 6:00 PM — Rio Nido Roadhouse
item.description:
Max Vogel is a country artist from Windsor, California, who has been singing and playing music his entire life. He picked up a guitar at 15 years old and hasn’t put it down since, spending years honing his craft as a singer, songwriter, and performer.
Inspired by artists like Garth Brooks, Alan Jackson, Randy Travis, Eric Church, Zac Brown Band, and Brooks & Dunn, Max blends traditional country roots with a modern edge. His music is built on honest storytelling, strong melodies, and the kind of songs that bring people together.
After many years performing as a solo artist, Max recently joined forces with a talented group of musicians to form Max Vogel & the Pickups. Together, they bring a high-energy country show filled with heartfelt originals, crowd-favorite country anthems, and a genuine connection with every audience they play for.
With a passion for music, family, and community, Max continues carving his path in the country music scene while keeping the spirit of country music

item.title: The Cemetery Club — Fri Jul 31, 8:00 PM — Bay Area Stage Theatre on Broadway
item.description:
Don’t be fooled by the title of this play – it’s a comedy!
Ivan Menchell’s The Cemetery Club is a bittersweet comedy about three Jewish widows in Queens, New York, who meet monthly to visit their husbands' graves. Their routine is upended when one of them begins dating a widower, who, they incidentally, meet at the cemetery. The ensuing drama tests their loyalties, offering a poignant look at love, friendship and moving on.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

….Get ready for the super-entertaining sounds of local band The Social Contractors. They totally rock, in all the right ways…” - Argus-Courier, 2025
The Social Contractors return to rock Spancky's Bar from 9 PM until midnight with their upbeat blend of original rock and tasteful interpretations of classic 60-90s hits from the bands you know and love \(Beatles, Hendrix, Pink Floyd, Cream, Stevie Wonder, Steve Miller, Foreigner, Police, Men At Work, Steely Dan, Tom Petty, Tears For Fears, U2, and more\).
Whether you like melodic vocals, searing guitar and sax solos, intriguing lyrics, captivating songs, or just great dynamic and danceable rhythms, The Social Contractors won't disappoint.
The Social Contractors lineup for this free live performance features band founder and songwriter, Jason E Davies \(lead vocals/lead guitar\), Travis Thayer \(sax/keys/vocals\), Rob Neidel \(bass/vocals\), and Chris \(drums\).

item.title: The MAC FREE August 1-2 with Bank of America Museums on Us — Sat Aug 1, 10:00 AM — Napa Valley Museum of Art and Culture
item.description:
Bank of America cardholders receive free general admission to participating museums nationwide on the first full weekend of each month; this month is August 1-2.
Looking for a chance to squeeze the last drop out of summer and beat the heat? The “MAC” \(Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture\) has exciting exhibits including My Andy: Photographs by Victoria Wyeth. Victoria, the only grandchild of Andrew and Betsy Wyeth, comes from a long lineage of painters, but chose photography. In the works on display for this exhibit, Victoria assiduously captured moments in her grandfather’s life—both intimate and spontaneous—that show a man at ease with himself and his family. She depicts his unique ability to inhabit the enchanted worlds he created. Victoria’s work is presented at The MAC as a companion to the exhibition “The Wyeths: Three Generations | Works from the Bank of America Collection,” complimenting and informing the paintings and drawings of her family.

item.title: Extended Run: Who Will Dance with Pancho Villa? — Fri Aug 7, 7:30 PM — The Raven Performing Arts Theater
item.description:
*Who Will Dance with Pancho Villa?* played to sold-out audiences in January. First performed off-Broadway in 1994, the playwrights updated the story with the introduction of the **Ballet Folklórico Legado de Mi Alegría de Cloverdale Ca** while developing the play further through the Raven Players’ ScripTease program. It is the story of a young Chicano from Chicago, lured to the East Coast by an Ivy League scholarship. As he tries to make a life there, he neglects family relationships and deep cultural roots established throughout generations. It takes his mother’s nearly fatal heart attack, help from a Jewish therapist, and the visitation of the spirits of his long dead relatives (and of his historical idol, Pancho Villa) to help him realize what he’s lost, and how to get it back. Dancing spirits, who are intertwined throughout the play, help remind “Chicano” of the joy in dancing, especially when dancing is much more than dancing.
By John and Gabriel Fraire
Directed by Jenna Vera Do
